questions.title: Vertebral level at which the rectum begins
questions.question: Regarding the rectum, which of the following statements is WRONG?

options.A: It is continuous above with the sigmoid colon
options.B: It is partly covered by peritoneum
options.C: It begins at the level of the first sacral vertebra (S1)
options.D: It is supplied by the superior, middle and inferior rectal arteries

explanations.A: Correct statement, so not the answer. The rectum is directly continuous above with the sigmoid colon at the rectosigmoid junction.
explanations.B: Correct statement, so not the answer. Peritoneum covers the front and sides of the upper third of the rectum and only the front of the middle third, while the lower third is entirely below the peritoneal reflection.
explanations.C: This is the wrong statement and therefore the answer. The rectum begins at the rectosigmoid junction in front of the third sacral vertebra (S3), not S1. It then descends along the curve of the sacrum and coccyx to end by piercing the pelvic diaphragm and becoming the anal canal. The S1 level marks the sacral promontory, well above the true origin of the rectum.
explanations.D: Correct statement, so not the answer. The rectum receives the superior rectal artery (from the inferior mesenteric), the middle rectal artery (from the internal iliac) and the inferior rectal artery (from the internal pudendal).

questions.module_subject: 206 DIG > Anatomy > Rectum and anal canal
questions.learning_objective: State that the rectum begins at the rectosigmoid junction in front of the S3 vertebra.

questions.title: Structure medial to the second part of the duodenum
questions.question: Which of the following structures lies medial to the second (descending) part of the duodenum?

options.D: Hepatic flexure of the colon

explanations.A: Correct. The second part of the duodenum descends to the right of the midline and curves around the head of the pancreas, which lies immediately medial to it in the concavity of the duodenal C-loop. The bile and main pancreatic ducts run in this groove and open into its posteromedial wall at the major duodenal papilla. This intimate relation is why carcinoma of the pancreatic head obstructs the bile duct and, when advanced, the duodenum itself.
explanations.B: Incorrect. The cystic duct lies above and to the right, running from the neck of the gall bladder to join the common hepatic duct, not medial to the descending duodenum.
explanations.C: Incorrect. The gall bladder is an anterior and superior relation of the first and second parts of the duodenum, not a medial one.
explanations.D: Incorrect. The hepatic (right colic) flexure of the colon is an anterior relation of the second part of the duodenum, lying in front of it rather than medial to it.

questions.learning_objective: Identify the head of the pancreas as the medial relation of the descending duodenum.

questions.title: Muscular sling around the anorectal junction
questions.question: Which of the following structures forms a U-shaped sling around the anorectal junction?

options.D: Puborectalis muscle

explanations.A: Incorrect. The sacrospinous ligament runs from the sacrum to the ischial spine and takes no part in the anorectal ring.
explanations.B: Incorrect. The anococcygeal ligament (body) is a midline raphe behind the anal canal between it and the coccyx; it anchors the canal but does not form a sling around it.
explanations.C: Incorrect. The superficial transverse perineal muscle lies in the superficial perineal pouch and stabilises the perineal body, not the anorectal junction.
explanations.D: Correct. The puborectalis is the most medial part of levator ani; its fibres pass from the pubis backwards around the anorectal junction as a U-shaped sling and rejoin the opposite side behind the gut. Its tone pulls the junction forward, creating the anorectal angle that is essential for faecal continence. Voluntary relaxation of this sling straightens the angle and permits defaecation.

questions.module_subject: 206 DIG > Anatomy > Rectum and anal canal
questions.learning_objective: Recognise the puborectalis sling and its role in the anorectal angle.

questions.title: Junction marked by the ligament of Treitz
questions.question: The ligament (suspensory muscle) of Treitz is the landmark of the:

options.D: Gastro-oesophageal junction

explanations.A: Correct. The suspensory muscle of the duodenum (ligament of Treitz) is a fibromuscular band that runs from the right crus of the diaphragm to the duodenojejunal flexure. It suspends and marks the duodenojejunal junction, the point at which the retroperitoneal duodenum becomes the mobile, mesentery-bearing jejunum. Surgeons use it intra-operatively to identify the start of the jejunum and to distinguish upper from lower gastrointestinal bleeding.
explanations.B: Incorrect. The ileocaecal junction is marked by the ileocaecal valve, not the ligament of Treitz.
explanations.C: Incorrect. The pyloroduodenal junction is marked externally by the prepyloric vein of Mayo, not the ligament of Treitz.
explanations.D: Incorrect. The gastro-oesophageal junction is marked by the cardiac orifice and the angle of His, not by the ligament of Treitz.

questions.learning_objective: Associate the ligament of Treitz with the duodenojejunal junction.

questions.title: Structure not on the anterior surface of the stomach
questions.question: Which of the following is NOT related to the anterior surface of the stomach?

options.D: Diaphragm

explanations.A: Correct, because it is the odd one out. The body of the pancreas is a posterior relation of the stomach, forming part of the stomach bed behind the lesser sac, not an anterior relation. The anterior (anterosuperior) surface of the stomach faces forwards and is related to the left lobe of the liver, the diaphragm and the anterior abdominal wall. The pancreas, together with the transverse mesocolon, spleen, left kidney and suprarenal gland, lies behind the stomach and is separated from it by the omental bursa.
explanations.B: Incorrect. The left lobe of the liver overlies the right part of the anterior surface of the stomach and is a genuine anterior relation.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Below the liver and costal margin the anterior surface of the stomach is in direct contact with the anterior abdominal wall.
explanations.D: Incorrect. The diaphragm is related to the upper part of the anterior surface of the stomach and separates it from the pleura, lung and pericardium.

questions.learning_objective: Distinguish the anterior relations of the stomach from its posterior bed.

questions.title: Structure lying on the base of the urinary bladder
questions.question: One of the following structures lies on the base (fundus) of the urinary bladder in the male:

options.D: Membranous urethra

explanations.A: Incorrect. The prostate lies below the bladder, surrounding the neck and the beginning of the urethra, not on the base.
explanations.B: Incorrect. The bulbourethral (Cowper's) glands lie in the deep perineal pouch, well below and behind the bladder.
explanations.C: Correct. The base (fundus) is the posteroinferior, triangular surface of the bladder that faces backwards and downwards. On each side of the midline the seminal vesicles rest against it, with the terminal ampullae of the vasa deferentia lying medial to them. Because only the peritoneum-free base separates the bladder from the seminal vesicles and the rectum, these structures can be palpated on rectal examination.
explanations.D: Incorrect. The membranous urethra is the short segment traversing the deep perineal pouch below the prostate, not a relation of the bladder base.

questions.learning_objective: Identify the seminal vesicle as a relation of the bladder base.

questions.title: Site of opening of the ejaculatory ducts
questions.question: The ejaculatory ducts open into the:

options.D: Navicular fossa

explanations.A: Correct. Each ejaculatory duct is formed behind the prostate by the union of the duct of the seminal vesicle with the ampulla of the vas deferens. The two ducts run forward and downward through the prostate to open on the seminal colliculus (verumontanum) of the prostatic urethra, one on each side of the prostatic utricle. This is why the prostatic urethra receives both the ejaculatory ducts and the prostatic ductules.
explanations.B: Incorrect. The membranous urethra is the sphincter-bearing segment in the deep perineal pouch and receives no ducts of significance.
explanations.C: Incorrect. The penile urethra receives the ducts of the bulbourethral glands and the small urethral (Littre) glands, not the ejaculatory ducts.
explanations.D: Incorrect. The navicular fossa is the dilated terminal part of the penile urethra in the glans and receives no ejaculatory ducts.

questions.learning_objective: State that the ejaculatory ducts open into the prostatic urethra.

questions.title: Origin and course of the vas deferens
questions.question: Regarding the ductus (vas) deferens, select the INCORRECT statement:

options.A: It begins as a continuation of the tail of the epididymis at the upper pole of the testis
options.B: It is palpable in the spermatic cord
options.C: It leaves the spermatic cord at the deep inguinal ring
options.D: The ampulla of the vas lies behind the base of the bladder

explanations.A: Correct, because this statement is false. The vas deferens does begin as the continuation of the tail (cauda) of the epididymis, but the tail lies at the LOWER pole of the testis, not the upper pole. From there the vas ascends on the medial side of the epididymis to enter the spermatic cord. Placing its origin at the upper pole reverses the true topography of the epididymis, whose head caps the upper pole and whose tail hangs from the lower pole.
explanations.B: Incorrect statement to choose, because it is true. The thick, cord-like vas is readily palpable between finger and thumb within the spermatic cord.
explanations.C: Incorrect statement to choose, because it is true. The vas leaves the other cord contents at the deep inguinal ring, hooks around the inferior epigastric artery and passes into the pelvis.
explanations.D: Incorrect statement to choose, because it is true. The dilated terminal ampulla of the vas lies on the base of the bladder, medial to the seminal vesicle.

questions.learning_objective: Trace the vas deferens from the tail of the epididymis at the lower testicular pole.

questions.title: Developmental origin of the renal glomeruli
questions.question: The glomeruli of the kidney are derived from the:

options.D: Mesonephric ducts

explanations.A: Incorrect. The ureteric bud forms the collecting system — the ureter, renal pelvis, calyces and collecting ducts — but not the glomeruli.
explanations.B: Incorrect. The paramesonephric (Mullerian) ducts form the female genital tract and regress in the male; they contribute nothing to the kidney.
explanations.C: Correct. The definitive kidney (metanephros) forms from two interacting tissues: the ureteric bud and the metanephric cap of mesenchyme (metanephric blastema) that condenses over its tip. The metanephric cap is induced to form the nephrons — the renal (Bowman's) capsule and glomerulus, proximal convoluted tubule, loop of Henle and distal convoluted tubule. The glomerular capillary tuft itself is invaginated into Bowman's capsule, so the glomerulus is a derivative of this metanephric mesenchyme.
explanations.D: Incorrect. The mesonephric (Wolffian) ducts give rise to the ureteric bud and, in the male, to the genital ducts, but not directly to the glomeruli.

questions.learning_objective: Attribute the nephron and glomerulus to the metanephric cap.

questions.title: Attachment of the apex of the urinary bladder
questions.question: Regarding the urinary bladder, select the TRUE statement:

options.A: Its epithelial lining is derived from ectoderm
options.B: Exstrophy of the bladder is due to persistence of the urachus
options.D: Its apex is connected to the umbilicus by the median umbilical ligament

explanations.A: Incorrect. The epithelium (transitional urothelium) of the bladder is of endodermal origin, derived from the vesical part of the urogenital sinus, not from ectoderm.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Exstrophy of the bladder results from failure of the infra-umbilical mesoderm to reinforce the anterior abdominal wall, so the wall and anterior bladder rupture; persistence of the urachus instead produces a urachal fistula, cyst or sinus.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Peritoneum covers the superior surface of the bladder and, when the bladder fills, is stripped upward off the anterior abdominal wall, allowing suprapubic puncture without entering the peritoneal cavity.
explanations.D: Correct. The apex of the bladder points forward toward the upper margin of the pubic symphysis and is continuous with the median umbilical ligament. This ligament is the fibrous remnant of the obliterated urachus (allantois) and runs upward in the extraperitoneal tissue to the umbilicus, raising the median umbilical fold of peritoneum. It anchors the apex of the bladder to the anterior abdominal wall.

questions.learning_objective: Relate the bladder apex to the median umbilical ligament (urachal remnant).

questions.title: Function of the seminal vesicle
questions.question: One of the following statements is FALSE regarding the seminal vesicle:

options.A: It lies on the posterior surface (base) of the bladder
options.B: Its medial surface is related to the ampulla of the vas deferens
options.C: It acts as a reservoir that stores spermatozoa
options.D: Its duct unites with the ductus deferens to form the ejaculatory duct

explanations.A: True statement, so not the answer. Each seminal vesicle is a lobulated sac lying against the base of the bladder, lateral to the ampulla of the vas and above the prostate.
explanations.B: True statement, so not the answer. The medial relation of the seminal vesicle is the terminal ampulla of the vas deferens on the same side.
explanations.C: This is the false statement and therefore the answer. Despite its name, the seminal vesicle is not a store of spermatozoa; sperm are stored mainly in the tail of the epididymis and the ampulla of the vas. The seminal vesicle is a secretory gland that produces an alkaline, fructose-rich fluid which nourishes the sperm and forms the bulk of the ejaculate. Its secretion is added to the sperm only at the moment of emission.
explanations.D: True statement, so not the answer. The duct of the seminal vesicle joins the ampulla of the vas deferens to form the ejaculatory duct.

questions.learning_objective: State that the seminal vesicle secretes seminal fluid and does not store sperm.

questions.title: Derivative of the pelvic part of the urogenital sinus
questions.question: In the male, the pelvic part of the urogenital sinus gives rise to the:

options.D: Upper part of the prostatic urethra

explanations.A: Correct. The urogenital sinus is divided into a vesical part (bladder), a pelvic part and a phallic part. In the male the narrow pelvic part forms the membranous urethra and the portion of the prostatic urethra below the openings of the ejaculatory ducts, and it induces the surrounding mesenchyme to form the prostate. The membranous urethra is therefore an endodermal derivative of the pelvic urogenital sinus.
explanations.B: Incorrect. The ejaculatory duct is a mesonephric (Wolffian) duct derivative, not a urogenital sinus derivative.
explanations.C: Incorrect. The seminal vesicle arises as an outgrowth of the mesonephric duct, not from the urogenital sinus.
explanations.D: Incorrect. The upper part of the prostatic urethra, above the entrance of the ejaculatory ducts, is derived from the mesonephric ducts, whereas the pelvic urogenital sinus forms the part below them and the membranous urethra.

questions.learning_objective: Assign the membranous urethra to the pelvic part of the urogenital sinus.

questions.title: Source of the internal spermatic fascia
questions.question: The internal spermatic fascia, a covering of the spermatic cord, is derived from the:

options.D: Fascia transversalis

explanations.A: Incorrect. The external oblique aponeurosis contributes the external spermatic fascia, taken from the margins of the superficial inguinal ring.
explanations.B: Incorrect. The internal oblique contributes the cremasteric muscle and fascia, not the internal spermatic fascia.
explanations.C: Incorrect. The transversus abdominis arches over the cord and forms part of the conjoint tendon; it does not contribute a covering to the cord.
explanations.D: Correct. As the developing testis and cord traverse the abdominal wall, each layer contributes a covering. The internal spermatic fascia is the innermost covering and is a prolongation of the fascia transversalis, picked up at the deep inguinal ring. Outside it lie the cremasteric fascia (from internal oblique) and the external spermatic fascia (from the external oblique aponeurosis).

questions.learning_objective: Derive the internal spermatic fascia from the fascia transversalis.

questions.title: Site of the upper ureteric constriction
questions.question: The ureter shows a normal anatomical constriction (a common site of stone impaction) at its upper end, at the:

options.D: Level of the twelfth thoracic (T12) vertebra

explanations.A: Incorrect. The middle third of the ureter runs over the pelvic brim and, while it may be narrowed where it crosses the iliac vessels, its upper constriction is not here.
explanations.B: Incorrect. The renal pelvis funnels down INTO the ureter; the narrowing is at the junction of the two, not above the pelvis.
explanations.C: Correct. The ureter has three normal constrictions where calculi tend to lodge: at the pelvi-ureteric junction (where the renal pelvis becomes the ureter), where it crosses the pelvic brim over the bifurcation of the common iliac artery, and where it pierces the bladder wall (the vesico-ureteric junction). The pelvi-ureteric junction is the uppermost and is a classic site of congenital obstruction and stone impaction.
explanations.D: Incorrect. The ureter begins at about the level of L1-L2 (transpyloric plane), not T12, and no constriction is described at T12.

questions.learning_objective: Locate the pelvi-ureteric junction as the upper ureteric constriction.

questions.title: Term for failure of testicular descent
questions.question: Failure of the testis to descend into the scrotum is referred to as:

options.D: Patent processus vaginalis

explanations.A: Correct. Cryptorchidism (undescended testis) is arrest of the testis anywhere along its normal path of descent, so that it lies in the abdomen, the inguinal canal or high in the scrotum rather than in its normal scrotal position. It is the commonest genital anomaly in male infants and carries an increased risk of infertility and malignancy if left uncorrected. The key feature is that the testis is on the normal line of descent but has not completed it.
explanations.B: Incorrect. An inguinal hernia is a protrusion of a peritoneal sac (often with gut) through the abdominal wall, which may accompany but is not the same as failure of testicular descent.
explanations.C: Incorrect. An ectopic testis has descended fully but come to lie OUTSIDE the normal path — for example in the superficial inguinal pouch, perineum or thigh — which is distinct from failed descent.
explanations.D: Incorrect. A patent processus vaginalis is persistence of the peritoneal diverticulum that precedes the testis; it predisposes to hernia and hydrocele but is not itself failure of descent.

questions.learning_objective: Define cryptorchidism as arrested testicular descent.

questions.title: Relations of the right ureter
questions.question: Regarding the right ureter, select the INCORRECT statement:

options.A: It is retroperitoneal throughout its course
options.B: In its abdominal course it is crossed by the right colic and gonadal vessels
options.C: It receives arterial branches from the renal artery
options.D: It is related medially to the inferior mesenteric vessels

explanations.A: True statement, so not the answer. The ureter is retroperitoneal along its whole abdominal and pelvic course.
explanations.B: True statement, so not the answer. The right ureter is crossed anteriorly by the right colic and ileocolic vessels, the gonadal vessels and the root of the mesentery.
explanations.C: True statement, so not the answer. The ureter has a segmental blood supply, its upper part receiving branches from the renal artery.
explanations.D: This is the false statement and therefore the answer. It is the LEFT ureter that is related medially to the inferior mesenteric vessels and is crossed by the left colic and sigmoid vessels. The right ureter lies to the right of the inferior vena cava and the root of the mesentery, so the inferior mesenteric vessels are not its medial relation. Confusing the two sides is the trap this question is built on.

questions.learning_objective: Contrast the abdominal relations of the right and left ureters.

questions.title: Widest and most dilatable part of the male urethra
questions.question: Which part of the male urethra is the widest and most dilatable?

options.D: Penile (spongy) urethra

explanations.A: Correct. The prostatic urethra, about 3 cm long as it passes through the prostate, is the widest and most dilatable part of the male urethra. Its posterior wall bears the urethral crest, the seminal colliculus with the prostatic utricle, and the openings of the ejaculatory ducts and prostatic ductules. Because it is wide and distensible it is the least likely part to be injured by instrumentation.
explanations.B: Incorrect. The preprostatic (intramural) urethra is a short segment at the bladder neck surrounded by the internal sphincter; it is not the widest part.
explanations.C: Incorrect. The membranous urethra is the shortest and narrowest and least dilatable part, surrounded by the external urethral sphincter in the deep perineal pouch.
explanations.D: Incorrect. The penile urethra is of intermediate calibre, dilating only at the intrabulbar fossa and the navicular fossa, and is longer but narrower than the prostatic part.

questions.learning_objective: Identify the prostatic urethra as the widest, most dilatable urethral segment.

questions.title: Features of the trigone of the urinary bladder
questions.question: Regarding the trigone of the urinary bladder, which statement is correct?

options.A: Its mucosa is thrown into folds when the bladder is empty
options.C: The internal urethral orifice lies at its apex, inferiorly
options.D: It lies on the inner aspect of the superior surface of the bladder

explanations.A: Incorrect. Unlike the rest of the bladder, the trigone mucosa is smooth and remains flat even when the bladder is empty because it is firmly bound to the underlying muscle.
explanations.B: Incorrect. The trigone develops from the absorbed ends of the mesonephric ducts, so it is mesodermal in origin (later re-lined by endodermal urothelium), not ectodermal.
explanations.C: Correct. The trigone is a smooth triangular area on the internal aspect of the base of the bladder. Its two posterosuperior angles are marked by the ureteric orifices, joined by the interureteric crest, and its single inferior angle (apex) is formed by the internal urethral orifice at the bladder neck. This constant, sensitive triangle is an important landmark at cystoscopy.
explanations.D: Incorrect. The trigone lies on the base (posteroinferior surface) of the bladder, not on its superior surface.

questions.learning_objective: Describe the trigone and locate the internal urethral orifice at its apex.

questions.title: Tributaries of the inferior vena cava
questions.question: Concerning the inferior vena cava, which statement is TRUE?

options.A: It commences at the level of the third lumbar vertebra (L3)
options.B: It has gastrointestinal tributaries corresponding to the gut branches of the aorta
options.C: It drains the whole of the venous return from the gut wall
options.D: The hepatic veins are among its tributaries

explanations.A: Incorrect. The inferior vena cava is formed by the union of the two common iliac veins at the level of the fifth lumbar vertebra (L5), not L3.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Unlike the aorta, the inferior vena cava has NO gastrointestinal tributaries; venous blood from the gut is carried instead by the portal system to the liver.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Blood from the gut wall drains into the portal vein, not directly into the inferior vena cava; it reaches the cava only after passing through the liver via the hepatic veins.
explanations.D: Correct. The tributaries of the inferior vena cava include the common iliac, lumbar, right gonadal, renal, right suprarenal, inferior phrenic and the hepatic veins. The hepatic veins are the last tributaries, opening into the cava just before it pierces the diaphragm. They deliver to the cava all the blood the liver has received from both the hepatic artery and the portal vein.

questions.module_subject: 206 DIG > Anatomy > Posterior abdominal wall vessels
questions.learning_objective: List the hepatic veins among the tributaries of the inferior vena cava.

questions.title: Features of the lower half of the anal canal
questions.question: Regarding the lower half of the anal canal (below the pectinate line), select the INCORRECT statement:

options.B: It is supplied by a somatic (spinal) nerve and is therefore sensitive to pain
options.C: It is drained by the inferior rectal vein
options.D: The sacrum and sacral plexus lie anterior to it

explanations.A: True statement, so not the answer. The lower half of the anal canal develops from the ectodermal proctodeum, which is why it is lined by stratified squamous epithelium.
explanations.B: True statement, so not the answer. It is supplied by the inferior rectal (somatic) nerve, so it is sensitive to pain, temperature and touch — the reason a thrombosed external pile is painful.
explanations.C: True statement, so not the answer. Its venous blood drains through the inferior rectal vein into the internal pudendal and internal iliac (systemic) veins.
explanations.D: This is the false statement and therefore the answer. The sacrum, coccyx and sacral plexus lie POSTERIOR to the anal canal and rectum, not anterior. Anterior relations are the perineal body, the bulb of the penis and the urethra (male) or the lower vagina (female). Reversing the anteroposterior relations is the error the option is built on.

questions.module_subject: 206 DIG > Anatomy > Rectum and anal canal
questions.learning_objective: State the posterior (sacral) and anterior relations of the anal canal.
